The committed driver is now driver_sha256_current: review rounds added (a) an explicit cm baseline, so a metre-unit session cannot compare centimetre OpenMaya values against working-unit cmds values, and a cm read that switches back to cm instead of to whatever the session used; (b) an explicit degree baseline, so a radian session cannot turn the 45 into 45 radians; (c) cleanup that deletes only the nodes the probe created, using the names Maya returned rather than a name substring; (d) DAG paths derived from those returned names instead of hardcoded strings, so a name clash can never touch the user's node; (e) os.path.join for the source path, so the driver also loads on Linux/macOS; (f) a root-namespace absolute name for the door, so a non-root current namespace cannot quietly drop it from the zone match. None of these can move a recorded number: the run's session was already in cm and degrees (restored_unit below, and the 141.4214 size proves degrees), so both forced baselines were no-ops, and the rest affect naming, path joining and cleanup only. The later revisions were syntax-checked and lint-clean but NOT executed against a live Maya (the session was closed). Re-running on a cm, degree scene must reproduce these rows.

rows.claim: Known limitation, measured not argued: the cached box is itself an AABB, so a rotation above the node can only over-approximate
rows.setup: parent rot Y30, child local rot Y-30 (world rotation is identity), 10 cube
rows.detail: The child's cached parent-space box is shaped by its own -30 rotation, so it is already wider than the 10-wide world box; multiplying it by the parent's +30 rotation keeps that extra width, and new_world_bbox comes out 18.66 wide against a true 10. This is the general property: _world_bbox reads a box that is itself an AABB, so any rotation applied above that space over-approximates unless the geometry fills the box it was measured in. Top-level nodes are exact because the exclusive matrix is the identity — which is why the 45-degree case in the issue is exact even though a rotated cube does not fill its cached AABB. The cure is to read the node's shapes instead of the cached transform box: one 8-corner transform per shape, exact for box-based geometry, with a vertex walk needed only for geometry that does not fill its box. #266 keeps the cached read on purpose (O(1)). Pinned by tests/test_maya_stub.py::TestSceneGraph::test_cached_box_cannot_be_un_rotated.

Cached-AABB limitation above: exact when no rotation sits above the node's cached box (or the geometry fills the box it was measured in), conservative otherwise. Pinned by tests/test_maya_stub.py::TestSceneGraph::test_cached_box_cannot_be_un_rotated; the cheap cure is walking the node's shapes.

Five raw MFnDagNode.boundingBox reads were left alone by this ticket: src/maya_mcp_server/maya_scene_module.py:~463 (spatial-index auto threshold, extents only), :~1000 (min_height/max_height, an internal-cm extent compared against a caller value that is not unit-converted), :~1560 (camera framing size; its extents also become the distance handed to cmds.move, which reads working units, so a metre scene frames 100x too far), src/maya_mcp_server/scene_tools.py:~464 (scene_inspect: the node's own box, in internal cm, next to a world position and a currentUnit label), and src/maya_mcp_server/asset_module.py:~402-419 (its own _world_bbox: exactWorldBoundingBox first, but the OpenMaya fallback repeats this ticket's double transform and is in internal cm). Rationale for leaving them: #266's scope is the zone/geometry read path, scene_inspect's space convention is now documented in README, and the extents-only sites do not suffer the double translate. The unit half of scene_inspect and asset_module's fallback, and the camera framing consequence, are the same defect class as #266 bug C. No follow-up issue has been filed yet.
get_scene_graph()'s payload declares `unit` from currentUnit while its p and b numbers stay internal centimetres. Unchanged by this ticket (b is now world space, still cm) and worth its own report.

measure() reports distance and overlap_dims in internal centimetres while the CoS formatter prints the scene unit next to them. Unchanged by this ticket; scene_tools' scene_measure description still promises the current linear unit.
